summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +6.2%; weakest: Lean hogs -22.8%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.85% (-15 bp in a month), 2-year 4.61% (-7 bp); 2s10s curve +24 bp (-8 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.16% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.66 (+1.3% in a month, +5.5% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.721 (+6.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.651 (-0.3%); USD/MXN 19.64 (+5.9%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -6.4% in a month (+4.9% YTD); VIX 26.9. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 84.43 $/bbl (-13.9% in a month), Brent 91.22, ULSD 3.679 $/gal (-18.7%), natural gas 3.62 (+4.5%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -19.2% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.7%, Hang Seng -3.5%, yuan +0.3% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 9 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (27%); S&P GSCI -14.2% in a month; gold -12.4%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
